name: Castmagic
summary: Turns recorded audio and video into a stack of ready-to-use assets: transcripts in 60+ languages, show notes, summaries, newsletters, social posts, clips and audiograms, with custom prompts and an AI chat across your whole library.
best_for: content teams, agencies and serious podcasters with a steady flow of recorded audio or video who want a transcript plus a stack of derived assets — show notes, newsletters, social posts, clips — from every upload, and who record enough hours to fill a tier
skip_if: you record occasionally, you only need an accurate transcript and nothing downstream of it, or you need a month-to-month price you can read off the page before you sign up
honest_knock:
The prices on the page are the annual prices. The toggle sits on “Annually — Save 30% Annually” by default, so $19, $48 and $139 are what you pay when you commit for a year. The month-to-month figures are readable in the page source and they are $29, $69 and $199, so the gap is real and on the entry tier it is wider than advertised: Hobby is about 34% cheaper annually, not 30%.

The hours are the part to pin down before you subscribe. The comparison table labels them “transcribed hours (library total)”, and the FAQ describes “a growing library of transcribed hours ... that you build up over time”. That wording fits a monthly allowance and a lifetime ceiling equally well, and the difference between the two is enormous. 30 hours every month at $19 is a bargain for a weekly podcast. 30 hours in total is about seven episodes, and then you are buying top-ups. Ask before you pay, and ask what happens to the hours when you downgrade.

And the social proof does not agree with itself — now in three directions. The pricing page says “75k+ Creators Served” and “75,000+ Creators & Businesses”; the homepage hero says “Loved by 100K+ podcasters and creators”; and the site's own llms.txt claims “200,000+ creators — including 100,000+ podcasters and 75,000+ creators and teams”. Three numbers, one site, and they cannot all be current. It is a small thing, and the kind of small thing that tells you which numbers on a marketing site have been checked recently. Treat the totals, the 10M minutes and the named logos as marketing, and judge the product on the trial.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-09-18 and again on 2026-10-05 on castmagic.io/pricing, every figure and both sets of data attributes unchanged) Three published tiers plus an enterprise band. The page opens on “Annually — Save 30% Annually”, and it now labels each card in words: “per month, billed annually”. Hobby $19 a month billed annually, $239 a year: 30 transcribed hours, up to 3 Spaces, 50GB storage, max team size 3 seats, no API access, no onboarding call, standard support. Starter $48 a month billed annually, $579 a year: 100 hours, 10 Spaces, 250GB, 5 seats, API access, onboarding call, standard support. Team $139 a month billed annually, $1,669 a year: 400 hours, 25 Spaces, 1TB, unlimited team size with 5 seats included and extras at $159 a year or $19 a month each, priority support. Business & Scale from $699 a month on annual billing and $999 a month on monthly billing, by demo, for custom volume, seats, storage, SLA and dedicated support. The monthly-billing prices ARE readable now, which they were not on 19 August 2026: the page carries both figures as data attributes on each amount and swaps them with script, giving Hobby $29, Starter $69 and Team $199 a month when billed monthly. Against the annual rates that is a 34% saving on Hobby and about 30% on Starter, Team and Business & Scale, so the “Save 30%” chip understates the entry tier. Unlimited AI outputs, re-generations, media clipping, audiograms, AI image generation, custom prompts, community prompts and 2000+ word outputs are on all three published tiers, as are 60+ transcription languages, unlimited file uploads, a 10GB maximum file size, 50 maximum concurrent uploads, the Media Library, and the Zoom, Google Drive, Zapier, RSS and YouTube/TikTok/Instagram imports. The hours still need care. The table calls them “transcribed hours (library total)” and the FAQ says every plan includes “a growing library of transcribed hours — 30 on Hobby, 100 on Starter, and 400 on Team — that you build up over time”, which still never states whether the allowance renews each month or is a running ceiling. Extra hours can be bought at any time on every tier, and the FAQ says you can upgrade or downgrade whenever you like. New on the site since 19 August 2026: Audience Chat (a chatbot for your own site trained on your episodes, citing the moment and capturing the lead), an API plus a Claude MCP server, an AI content strategist, async interviews, carousels and vertical clips, and a claim of “130+ tools”.
